page: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 32-core AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. Configured on the AWS Nitro System, this arm64 server features 32 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core and 64 GB of system memory, providing a 2 GB per core memory allocation. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. The instance lacks local block storage and integrated GPU acceleration, but delivers a baseline network throughput of 17 Gbps alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions.

Benchmark results highlight exceptionally strong single-core and multi-core processor performance, particularly in software compilation, text processing, and data compression workloads. The instance achieves top-tier scores in Geekbench single-core, multi-core, and Clang code compilation benchmarks, as well as high memory score and database operation results in PassMark testing. Redis SET throughput reaches 93.19 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 92.57 GB/sec. However, raw single-core execution in stress-ng tests and uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidth fall into average benchmark ranges. Additionally, small-model language model text generation and medium-model prompt processing demonstrate moderate performance, while memory-heavy or GPU-dependent tasks remain constrained by the 2 GB per core RAM profile and absence of dedicated hardware accelerators.

The c9g.8xlarge offers solid resource density for compute-intensive workloads that require dedicated physical execution threads rather than hyperthreaded virtual cores. With a balanced 2:1 ratio of memory to core count, the server maximizes processing capacity per resource footprint for highly parallel execution. This architecture provides strong efficiency for software compilation, CI/CD pipelines, high-concurrency web serving, Redis key-value caching, in-memory processing, and general-purpose microservice architectures.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 32-core AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor operating at 3.3 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores, 64 GB of RAM, 48 MB of L3 cache, AES cryptographic acceleration, and a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps, without bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier execution in software compilation with Clang, text processing, single-threaded compression, static web serving throughput, and database operations. It also delivers strong multi-core processing in Geekbench and high Redis SET transaction rates. The 2 GB per core RAM allocation limits memory-intensive applications, while uncached memory bandwidth and single-core stress testing perform at average levels. The architecture provides high compute density for parallel workloads such as CI/CD pipelines, high-throughput web servers, Redis caches, and distributed application microservices.

bullet_points: Powered by a 32-core ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 CPU at 3.3 GHz with dedicated physical cores.
Equipped with 64 GB of RAM (2 GB per vCPU) and 17 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.
Features hardware AES cryptographic acceleration and 48 MB of L3 cache without bundled local storage.
Top-tier performance in software compilation, data compression, static web serving, and database operations.
Strong transaction throughput reaching 93.19 million SET operations per second in Redis.
Optimized for CI/CD build environments, microservices, key-value stores, and parallel compute tasks.
